findings.summary: Cursor did not produce the required artifact
15 commit(s) on 'claude/por-stat-classification' not in main — fixes are written but not deployed

AI input screening uses `sentinel.action.quarantine_artifact` both to read signals and quarantine artifacts, combining collection with broker capability; there are only seven unique named identities across eight sections because agent health and cost share a scope.

SENSITIVE_PII and secrets are not demonstrably unreachable: unrestricted header values, actor identity, replication error strings, and artifact references lack mandatory sanitization and could carry cookies, personal identifiers, credentials, or source text.

Auto actions are not defined with enforceable scope, reversal, TTL, and idempotency semantics; rate limits, task pauses, retry stops, snapshot trust changes, notifications, and quarantines lack one or more required properties.

Analyst-to-collector and analyst-to-broker isolation is asserted but no identity inventory, ACL, process boundary, broker authorization protocol, or runtime evidence establishes it; the analyst also directly emits proposals toward the broker.

The HEALTHY state has no required evidence source, freshness threshold, transition rule, or fail-closed behavior when watchdog evidence is absent, so the document does not prevent an unsupported HEALTHY report.

No process/account/key/token/write-role/queue/release-approval/health-monitor sharing is asserted but not confirmed by inventories, deployment definitions, credential bindings, queue ACLs, or runtime evidence.
Injection screening includes the issue title, but the unsanitized title is still copied into the agent-consumed objective, contradicting quarantine guarantees.
Routing applies labels sequentially with last-label-wins semantics, so conflicting labels such as p0 and p2 produce different risk tiers depending on GitHub label order instead of failing closed.
A control-plane task creation failure is placed in skipped, but the final bridge health still reports state OK and READ_SUCCEEDED.
The full operational inventory is gated only by readSession(), not requireApiAuth as required by the objective.
No HTTP session can map to MANAGER; the cited test calls matterHttpGate directly, so it does not prove that a MANAGER-role session is refused por-write by requireApiAuth.
requireApiAuth maps each permission to a fixed read action, and no application mapping uses por-write, so mutating HTTP operations are not classified by their actual action/resource risk.
The HTTP boundary does not use the stated security-gateway engine; it uses a divergent TypeScript copy where inventory-read is tier 1 instead of tier 2 and role/agent policies differ materially.

Collector-supplied signalIds are accepted as arbitrary strings, bypass text redaction, returned by APIs, and displayed in the owner drilldown, so secrets or PII can leak despite the counts-only claim.
TLS metadata and dependency advisory IDs are readable despite no named TLS or dependency-vulnerability detection, contradicting the rule that every readable field is required by a named detection.

Bridge tests reproduced 14/14, but gateway execution stopped after one assertion because it writes SECURITY_AUDIT.jsonl, while the sentinel suite is also filesystem-mutating; only static counts of 14 and 25 assertions were independently established.
npm run test:security exits nonzero during the Matter gateway test with EPERM, while health-specific checks only inspect source text and do not execute authenticated and unauthenticated requests.
SECURITY_AUDIT.jsonl contains the claimed decisions, but they were generated by direct unit calls labeled matter_http rather than demonstrated authenticated HTTP requests.
A HEALTHY watchdog timestamp arbitrarily far in the future is treated as fresh because only ages greater than 15 minutes are rejected; negative ages are accepted.

npm run test:security did not pass end-to-end: the tsx CLI was blocked by IPC permissions, and loader-based execution exposed a failing Matter audit assertion, so the expected regression result is not established.
